title: Husbands — Vivienne VIV_01 Timing Budget & Phrase Continuity Profile
status: SUPERSEDED_BY_VIV_01_CALIBRATION_ANALYSIS_V2 — LEGACY TIMING AND PHRASE NOTES RETAINED
purpose: Turn VIV_01 source-vs-TTS speech-boundary screening into cue-level timing review and phrase-continuity instructions. This is not a claim of human listening approval.
principles: Do not force one fixed speaking rate on Vivienne. Choose local pacing per phrase from source acting intent, Mongolian syllable load, urgency, and available non-overlap window.

Do not blindly force Mongolian active speech duration to equal English VAD duration; Mongolian translation may be longer. Preserve meaning and natural articulation while fitting the actual scene window.

Keep the existing ElevenLabs voice ID, model, and saved numerical settings unchanged during this validation stage. Adjust text phrasing, cue-level performance direction, and timing placement before considering global settings.
Use source VAD as a timing reference only. It is not phoneme alignment, and music/effects/breaths can affect VAD.
Do not use MP3 container duration as speech duration; use decoded speech-active boundaries and separately inspect leading/trailing silence.
Separate subtitle cue assets may still need phrase-level continuity. Avoid an artificial reset or full pause at cue boundaries when the sentence continues.
Preserve original subtitle text and timestamps unless a separately reviewed subtitle correction is approved.
No paid TTS request is authorized by this profile.

findings.interpretation: A flagged overrun is a scheduling risk if the clip is placed at its subtitle start; it is not proof of audible collision. Confirm against the next speaker's actual dialogue onset and the scene edit.

phrase_groups.instruction: Maintain one connected thought; use short natural transitions, not three isolated sentence reads. Cue 1 requires faster/leaner articulation to reduce timing risk without sounding rushed.

Treat as one syntactic phrase across two cue assets. Cue 5 is only 0.8 s subtitle slot and overlaps the following Lucian dialogue risk; do not let its audio spill into Lucian. Prioritize compact natural delivery and verify exact scene speech onset.

phrase_groups.function: One continuous thought with clause completion
phrase_groups.instruction: Cue 10 has an internal pause flag; avoid inserting a dramatic pause unless source acting supports it.

phrase_groups.function: Three-step emotional progression in inner monologue
phrase_groups.instruction: Keep progression connected. Cue 18 is the most forceful semantic phrase but do not infer anger tag from text alone; user-approved scene map remains authoritative.
Cue 24 has the major pause anomaly. Preserve the source's concise transition; do not create a long internal gap. Cue 23 and 24 need careful timing review.

phrase_groups.function: One sentence split across adjacent cues
phrase_groups.instruction: No full stop or fresh emotional reset at cue 28/29 boundary; preserve breath and syntax continuity.

phrase_groups.function: Continuous explanatory narration about the contract
phrase_groups.instruction: Use measured explanatory pacing with clear contrast/emphasis only where meaning requires it. Avoid making every cue a separate declarative performance.
Keep descriptive phrases compact and connected. Cue 38 timing risk is high; avoid excess trailing pause.

phrase_groups.function: Short dialogue exchange followed by narration
phrase_groups.instruction: Cues 51 and 52 are character dialogue, not narration. Preserve conversational turn continuity and ensure cue 52 finishes before cue 53 begins; do not apply narration pacing to these lines.

production_workflow: For each cue, inspect the English source interval and identify speech onset/end, pause positions, stress, and phrase continuation.
Estimate Mongolian spoken duration from actual VAD speech-active time, not MP3 file length.
Set a cue-specific timing budget bounded by the next speaker's verified onset; if the translation cannot fit naturally, revise timing/edit placement rather than accelerate to an unnatural rate.
Use phrase groups to coordinate delivery across separate cue assets; maintain continuous prosody across cue boundaries.
Listen to all flagged VIV_01 MP3s against the source before approving any re-generation or final mix.
Only after the user approves a named batch and paid request count may new ElevenLabs requests be made.
